INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS

UNITED NATIONS (UN)

  • Established: 24 October 1945
  • Headquarters: New York, USA
  • Forerunner organisation: League of Nations formed by Treaty of Versailles, 1919
  • Formed at UN Conference on International Organization, 1945
  • Original Signatories: 50 countries + 1 (Poland signed later)
  • Logo: Globe, olive branches
  • Term coined by Franklin Roosevelt
  • Secretary-General: António Guterres (Portugal)
  • Total Countries: 193
  • Objective: Maintain international peace and security, develop friendly relations among nations, and achieve international cooperation.
  • Official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish

Principal Organs Of The United Nations

#### 1. UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY

  • Includes all UN Members
  • Two-thirds majority needed for major decisions, otherwise a simple majority
  • Decisions not binding on UN members
  • Key functions: Approves the UN budget, appoints the Secretary-General, makes recommendations through resolutions.

#### 2. UN SECURITY COUNCIL

  • Total 15 members
  • 5 Permanent Members (with veto power) are: Britain, France, China, USA, Russia
  • 10 Non-Permanent Members elected for a two-year term. (Originally 6) India has been a member 8 times
  • Japan: elected as a non permanent member most number of times.

#### 3. UN ECONOMIC and SOCIAL COUNCIL

  • Promotes international economic and social cooperation
  • 54 members elected for three-year terms

#### 4. UN INTERNATIONAL COURT OF JUSTICE

  • Judicial organ of the UN.
  • Located in The Hague, Netherlands
  • 15 judges elected for 9-year terms
  • successor of Permanent Court of International Justice (estd: 1920) under League of Nations

#### 5. UN TRUSTEESHIP COUNCIL

  • suspended on 1 Nov, 1994 with independence of Palau

#### 6. UN SECRETARIAT

  • Headed by the Secretary-General appointed for 5 year term.
  • Implements UN policies, administers peacekeeping operations, and prepares reports.

UN FUNDS AND PROGRAMMES

#### United Nations International Children's Fund (UNICEF)

  • Established: 11 December 1946
  • Headquarters: New York, USA
  • Objective: Provide humanitarian aid to children worldwide.
  • Key Focus: Child nutrition, education, immunization.

#### United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)

  • Established: 5 June 1972
  • Headquarters: Nairobi, Kenya
  • Founded by: UN General Assembly (at Stockholm Conference)
  • UNEP + World Meteorological Organization = IPCC in 1988 (IPCC - Inter Governmental Panel on Climate Change)

#### United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

  • Established: 1965
  • Headquarters: New York
  • Important reports by UNDP are:
  • Human Development Report
  • Gender Inequality Index
  • Global Multidimensional Poverty Index
  • Key Focus: poverty eradication, inclusive growth, reduce inequalities, achieve SDGs.

#### United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat)

  • Established: 1977
  • Headquarters: Nairobi, Kenya

#### World Food Programme (WFP)

  • Established: 1961
  • Headquarters: Rome, Italy
  • WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.

INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS

Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO)

  • Established: 1945
  • Headquarters: Rome, Italy

United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)

  • Established: 1969
  • Headquarters: New York

United Nations High Commissioner For Refugees (UNHCR)

  • Established: 1950
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Provides support and protection to refugees worldwide.
  • Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981

International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)

  • Established: 1947, Chicago Convention
  • Headquarters: Montreal, Canada

International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)

  • Established: 1977
  • Headquarters: Rome, Italy

OTHER SPECIALISED AGENCIES OF THE UN

#### International Labour Organization (ILO)

  • Established: 1919 (through the Treaty of Versailles)
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Received Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.

#### International Maritime Organization (IMO)

  • Established: 1948
  • Headquarters: London, UK
  • Focuses on maritime safety and environmental protection.
Established as Inter-Governmental Maritime Consultative Organization (IMCO) in 1948; became a specialized agency of the United Nations in 1959; renamed as International Maritime Organization in 1982.

#### International Monetary Fund (IMF)

  • Established: 1944 (Bretton Woods Conference)
  • Headquarters: Washington, D.C., USA
  • Works to ensure global monetary cooperation and financial stability.
  • Uses SDR (Special Drawing Rights) as its reserve asset/currency
  • SDR- Basket of 5 currencies: US Dollar, Yen, Euro, Pound and Renminbi.

#### World Bank

  • Established: 1944 (Bretton Woods Conference)
  • Headquarters: Washington, D.C., USA
  • The World Bank is a group of following 5 institutions:
  • IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
  • IDA (International Development Association)
  • IFC (International Finance Corporation)
  • MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency)
  • ICSID (International Centre of Settlement of Investment Disputes)
IMF & World Bank are known as Twin Organisations.

#### International Telecommunication Union (ITU)

  • Established: 1865
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Regulates international communication and radio frequencies.

#### United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

  • Established: 1945
  • Headquarters: Paris, France
  • Promotes education, science, and cultural heritage protection.

#### United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)

  • Established: 1966
  • Headquarters: Vienna, Austria
  • Supports industrial growth in developing nations.

#### World Health Organization (WHO)

  • Established: 7 April 1948 (celebrated as World Health Day)
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Works on global health initiatives, disease prevention, and medical research.

#### United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

  • Established: 1964
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Focuses on trade, investment, and development issues.

#### United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)

  • Established: 1997
  • Headquarters: Vienna, Austria
  • Works against drug trafficking, corruption, and international crime.

#### World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

  • Established: 1967
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Releases Global Innovation Index alongwith INSEAD, Cornell University.

#### International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)

  • Established: 1957
  • Headquarters: Vienna, Austria
  • Promotes the peaceful use of nuclear energy and ensures nuclear safety.

INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS

United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP)

  • Established: 1947
  • Headquarters: Bangkok, Thailand
  • Works on regional development, economic growth, and social issues in Asia-Pacific.

World Trade Organization (WTO)

  • Established: 1995 (through the Marrakesh Agreement, 1994)
  • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Regulates international trade between nations
  • Replaced GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade), established in 1948.
  • GATT had 23 member countries, WTO has 166 member countries, currently.
  • Current Director-General: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria)

REGIONAL ORGANISATIONS

#### South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)

  • Established: 8 December 1985 (Dhaka, Bangladesh)
  • Headquarters: Kathmandu, Nepal
  • Aims to promote economic and regional integration in South Asia.
  • Total Members: 8 (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Maldives).
  • Observers: 9 countries

#### Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)

  • Established: 8 August 1967 (Bangkok, Thailand)
  • Headquarters: Jakarta, Indonesia
  • Focuses on political, economic, and security cooperation in Southeast Asia.
  • Members: 10 (Malaysia, Brunei, Myanmar, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Laos, Cambodia)

#### Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical & Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)

  • Established: 1997
  • Headquarters: Dhaka, Bangladesh
  • Member Countries: 7 (Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, SriLanka, Thailand, Nepal, Bhutan)
  • 1st BIMSTEC Youth Summit was held in Gandhinagar, Gujarat in February 2025.

BRICS

  • Established: 2009, Russia
  • Member Countries: 10
  • Headquarters: Shanghai
  • BRICS is acronym where:
  • B: Brazil
  • R: Russia
  • I: India
  • C: China
  • S: South Africa (joined in 2010)
  • 5 New Members Added in 2023- Saudi Arabia, Egypt, United Arab Emirates (UAE), Ethiopia, Iran, making it BRICS+
  • While 6 countries were invited to join BRICS in 2023, only 5 joined, Argentina declined the invitation in December 2023 after a change in government.
  • So as of January 2024, BRICS has 10 members.
New Development Bank was established by BRICS countries in 2014, Headquarters: Shanghai, China.

Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)

  • Established: 2001 (by China & Russia)
  • Headquarters: Beijing, China
  • Member Countries: 10 (China, Russia, India, Pakistan (joined in 2017), Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran, Belarus (joined in 2024)

Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)

  • A Counter-Terrorism body under the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).
  • Established: 2002
  • Headquarters: Tashkent, Uzbekistan
  • Member Countries: 9 (As part of SCO)

Asian Development Bank (ADB)

  • Established: 1966
  • Headquarters: Manila, Philippines
  • Member Countries: 69 (India is a founding member of ADB)
  • India started availing of ADB's assistance in 1986.

European Union (EU)

  • Established: November 1, 1993 in Maastricht, Netherlands
  • Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium
  • Member Countries: 27 (After Brexit in 2020)
  • Awarded the Nobel Prize in 2012.
  • Has a Eurozone where countries adopt the Euro as currency
  • Total Eurozone Countries: 20
  • Latest Member: Croatia (Joined in 2023).
The European Economic Community (EEC), a precursor to the European Union was established in 1958 through the Treaty of Rome.

INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS

North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)

  • Established: 1949 (Through the North Atlantic Treaty)
  • Member Countries: 32
  • Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium
  • Military Headquarters: Mons, Belgium
  • Latest Member: Sweden (joined in March, 2024)

Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO)

  • Established: After the USSR Disintegration in 1991
  • Member Countries: 6 (Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan)

International Solar Alliance (ISA)

  • Established: 30 November, 2015 (Paris, France)
  • Headquarters: Gurugram, Haryana
  • Founding members: India & France
  • Concept: Proposed by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015 at Wembley Stadium, UK. He referred to Sunshine Countries as "Suryaputra" (Sons of the Sun).
  • Launch Event: India Africa Summit
  • Opened for signature in Marrakesh Morocco.
  • Number of Member Countries: 120+
  • Present Director General: Ashish Khanna

Group of Twenty (G20)

  • Established: 1999
  • Member Countries: 21 (19 countries + European Union + African Union)
  • Latest Member Joined: African Union, September 2023 (G20 India)
  • Current Presidency (2024-25): Brazil
  • Next Presidency (2025-26): South Africa
  • Major Annual Event: G20 Leaders' Summit
  • G20 countries account for 85% of the world GDP and more than 2/3rd of the total world's population.
G20 in India: 2023
- Theme: "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" (One Earth, One Family, One Future)
- G20 Summit Venue: New Delhi, Bharat Mandapam
- G20 Sherpa for India: Amitabh Kant
G20 Countries (flags shown): Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Republic of Korea, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Türkiye, United Kingdom, United States of America, European Union, African Union.

G7 (Group of Seven)

  • Established: 1975
  • Members: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, United Kingdom (Britain), United States, and the European Union. (TRICK: BF JUICE)
  • EU participates but does not hold presidency.
G20 & G7 have no permanent secretariat/office.

G8 (Group of Eight)

  • Established: 1997 (when Russia joined G7)
  • Members: G7 + Russia
  • Dissolution: Suspended in 2014 after Russia's annexation of Crimea, reverting back to G7.

Financial Action Task Force (FATF)

  • Established: 1989 (Initiative of G7 Countries)
  • Headquarters: Paris, France
  • Blacklist Countries: North Korea, Iran, and Myanmar
Promotes effective implementation of legal measures to combat money laundering, terrorist financing etc.

International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL)

  • Established: 1923
  • Headquarters: Lyon, France
  • Provides a platform for law enforcement agencies to collaborate, even between countries without diplomatic relations.

INTERPOL NOTICES

  • RED NOTICE: Arrest warrant
  • YELLOW NOTICE: Missing person
  • BLUE NOTICE: Additional information
  • BLACK NOTICE: Unidentified body
  • GREEN NOTICE: Warnings and intelligence
  • ORANGE NOTICE: Person of threat
  • PURPLE NOTICE: Modus operandi
  • INTERPOL-UN SECURITY COUNCIL SPECIAL NOTICE: Groups and individuals subject to UN sanctions

Bharatpol

  • Developed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), this portal allows both central and state agencies to connect with INTERPOL for real-time information sharing.
  • Replaces the previous system where only the CBI had direct access to INTERPOL.

World Economic Forum (WEF)

  • Established: 1971
  • Headquarters: Cologny, Switzerland

Important reports released by World Economic Forum

  1. 1. Global Risks Report
  2. 2. Global Competitiveness Report
  3. 3. Global Gender Gap Report
  4. 4. Global Travel and Tourism Report
  5. 5. Energy Transition Index

SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS

  • 17 Sustainable Development Goals (visual reference; key goals include: 1 No Poverty, 2 Zero Hunger, 3 Good Health and Well-Being, 4 Quality Education, 5 Gender Equality, 6 Clean Water and Sanitation, 7 Affordable and Clean Energy, 8 Decent Work and Economic Growth, 9 Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, 10 Reduced Inequalities, 11 Sustainable Cities and Communities, 12 Responsible Consumption and Production, 13 Climate Action, 14 Life Below Water, 15 Life on Land, 16 Peace and Justice Strong Institutions, 17 Partnerships for the Goals).
